data.title: So what is this thing, anyway?
data.tldr: The point of what Kestrel is, and what I want it is designed to do.
contents: ## Active vs. Passive

Looking at todays defensive posture, most solutions are compliance, signature and reactionary. Everyone speaks about active defense, and kill-chains, but I have yet to see anything that really fits the bill.
## Why bother

You get a pile of alerts, you read them on Monday, and by then whoever it was has been wandering around the house for days. I wanted the opposite of that. Something watching while it happens, that can act on its own instead of waiting for a person to scroll past the right line.
## The part I actually care about

One strange thing on its own is usually nothing. People log in late. Scripts do odd stuff. Files change. Chasing every single one of those is how good people burn out, and it is why so many alerts get ignored.

But a handful of small strange things, in the same short window, on the same machine, all pointing the same direction? That is a story. That is the thing worth catching, and it is what the whole project is built around: adding up little hints until they cross the line into 'okay, somebody should look at this'.
## Where the framework fits in

This is where yesterday connects to today. The MITRE ATT&CK® framework is basically a catalog of the moves attackers actually make, written down by people who have watched them happen. Kestrel comes preloaded with that catalog, so it is not guessing at what 'suspicious' means. It is comparing what it sees against behavior somebody already documented. The [ATT&CK® Visualized](visualized.html) page is my attempt to look at that whole catalog at once.
## The goal

Fewer alerts nobody reads, and more decisions that actually get made. If this works the way I want, the boring stuff stays quiet and the real thing gets caught early enough to still matter. That is the entire goal. Everything else is detail.

data.title: The Journey begins
data.tldr: This started as a simple 'I want to see how the pieces of the MITRE ATT&CK® framework fit together' and turned into a much bigger question: what does 'practical application of defense' actually mean?
contents: ## A bit like Alice, tumbling down the Rabbit hole

There is a difference between knowing *of* something and actually knowing it. That gap is where I kept getting stuck, along with the obvious follow-up question: how is any of this supposed to make sense?
## Visual Learning

So I did what anyone would do and started clicking around the Enterprise framework, poking at each category to see what its properties were. It made sense on the surface, but the questions kept piling up. How do I make this click for me? How does a tactic actually connect to a technique? How do those connect to their analytics and data components? Where do the data components overlap? Are they built on passive logging only? And what other Linux events and telemetry are out there that nobody talks about?
## Researching

Doing research well is slow, and honestly kind of a grind. Big thanks to the folks at MITRE for pulling all of this together and publishing it in more than one format so regular people can actually use it. Thank you, nameless heroes!
Because the data ships as JSON, I could filter it down to the topics I cared about and build a visualization that shows how everything relates.
## Enjoy

The first step is always understanding what you are looking at, and that step never really ends. I hope these visualizations, starting with [ATT&CK® Visualized](visualized.html), help other people make sense of this stuff too.
